confirmed.quote: The sign agrees on 4 of 4 models and the magnitude within a factor of five on 4, with the ratio running 0.71 to 3.30. ... That is a different object from two weak results pointing the same way. It is one channel with a predicted magnitude that two estimators built on different subsets of the grid agree on, which is the same form of check §6.2 applies to the Jacobian and the one that would have exposed the channel as spurious had the numbers not matched. (§4.4, Table 10)
confirmed.defect: The two estimators are not independent and their agreement is largely forced by construction, so the check has almost no power to expose a spurious channel. The predicted shift is -b*mean(Δ) where b is the OLS slope of the per-pair effect y on Δ; the observed shift is mean(y | Δ=0) - mean(y). Because the token-matched subset IS the Δ=0 subset, both are linear functionals of the same 48 y-values and are positively correlated under the null: if the Δ=0 pairs happen to sit low by chance, b is pushed positive and the predicted shift negative, which is the same sign as the observed shift. The paper explicitly denies this ("Neither is used to compute the other, so the comparison can fail") and no null calibration is reported anywhere. This corroboration is load-bearing: the primary test on this channel straddles 0.05 (bootstrap p=0.078, exact relabel p=0.045, row-level p=0.003), so Table 10 is what the section leans on.
confirmed.evidence: Recomputed from paper-a/data/names/names_*.jsonl and paper-a/data/instrument/name_length_<model>.json. Because the slope b is fitted on ALL 48 pairs — a set that CONTAINS the token-matched rows — the identity mean(y | Δ=0) − mean(y) = −b·Δ̄ + mean(residual | Δ=0) holds exactly, so 'observed shift' minus 'predicted shift' is identically the mean OLS residual on the matched rows. The two quantities are not built on different subsets and cannot be independent. The check therefore only asks whether the matched-subset residual is small, and it is not: on Llama-2-7B-chat and Mistral v0.1 the residual is 2.15× and 2.30× the predicted shift, i.e. 68 % and 70 % of the observed shift is unexplained by the length slope. Table 10's caption 'Neither quantity enters the other's computation' is false as a statement of independence.
